How often does a dog licensed in New York City have a name that was popular among U.S. babies? We group the 2024 licenses into estimated dogs, then compare their names with the U.S. top 100 in three decades.

## From licenses to estimated dogs
### Read the license records
NYC supplies the column headers. We read the fields as text to keep leading zeros in ZIP codes and to preserve names as written. For example, the city uses the two letters `NA` as one way to mark a missing name.

```{r}
#| label: read-license-records
library(tidyverse)

sources <- read_csv("data/sources.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
dogs_raw <- read_csv(
  "data/raw/nyc-dogs-2024.csv",
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
  na = character(), trim_ws = FALSE
)
missing_labels <- read_csv(
  "data/lookups/missing_name_labels.csv",
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character()), na = character()
)
```

### Give the license fields clear names
`rename()` changes the heading above each column. Every field in this step gets an `original_` prefix so we can see what came from the city. The row number tells us which license supplied each value.

```{r}
#| label: name-license-columns
dogs_raw |>
  rename(
    original_name = animalname,
    original_sex = animalgender,
    original_birth_year = animalbirth,
    original_breed = breedname,
    original_zipcode = zipcode,
    original_issue_date = licenseissueddate,
    original_expiry_date = licenseexpireddate,
    original_extract_year = extract_year
  ) |>
  mutate(source_row_id = row_number()) ->
  dogs_original
```

```{r}
#| label: preview-original-licenses
preview <- function(records) {
  records |>
    slice_head(n = 6)
}

dogs_original |>
  preview()
```

### Identify missing names
Our lookup lists six ways the city recorded a missing name, including `UNKNOWN` and `NA`. We match them before changing any spelling. We keep `BABY` as a name.

```{r}
#| label: label-missing-names
dogs_original |>
  left_join(missing_labels, by = c("original_name" = "recorded_name")) ->
  dogs_labeled
```

### Normalize formatting
We give every full name the same spelling for matching by uppercasing it and removing spaces and hyphens. For example, `WALL-E` becomes `WALLE`. We keep the original name and ZIP alongside their matching forms. Sex, birth year and breed carry over as recorded. We also turn the license dates into dates we can sort.

```{r}
#| label: normalize-formatting
dogs_labeled |>
  mutate(
    sex = original_sex, birth_year = original_birth_year, breed = original_breed,
    name_status = replace_na(name_status, "recorded"),
    name_missing = name_status == "not_recorded",
    name_key = str_to_upper(original_name, locale = "en"),
    zipcode_contains_one_to_five_digits = str_detect(original_zipcode, "^[0-9]{1,5}$"),
    zipcode_with_leading_zeros = str_pad(original_zipcode, width = 5, pad = "0"),
    license_issue_date = str_sub(original_issue_date, 1, 10),
    license_expiry_date = str_sub(original_expiry_date, 1, 10),
    extract_year = as.integer(original_extract_year),
    breed_label = str_trim(breed),
    birth_year_number = as.integer(birth_year)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    name_key = str_remove_all(name_key, "[\\s-]"),
    license_issue_date = parse_date(license_issue_date),
    license_expiry_date = parse_date(license_expiry_date),
    breed_label = str_to_upper(breed_label)
  ) ->
  dogs_formatted
```

```{r}
#| label: normalize-formatting-preview
dogs_formatted |>
  select(original_name, name_key, original_zipcode, license_issue_date) |>
  preview()
```

### Flag uncertain fields
We flag compounds using the spelling on the license. We also mark records with an unknown breed or sex, a questionable birth year or a ZIP that cannot be written as five digits. These licenses still count.

```{r}
#| label: flag-uncertain-fields
dogs_formatted |>
  mutate(
    name_key = if_else(name_missing, NA_character_, name_key),
    compound_name = !name_missing & str_detect(original_name, "\\S\\s+\\S|[^\\s-]-[^\\s-]"),
    zipcode = if_else(zipcode_contains_one_to_five_digits, zipcode_with_leading_zeros, original_zipcode),
    zipcode_padded = zipcode != original_zipcode,
    zipcode_invalid = !str_detect(zipcode, "^[0-9]{5}$"),
    breed_unknown = breed_label %in% c("", "UNKNOWN"),
    birth_year_has_four_digits = str_detect(birth_year, "^[0-9]{4}$"),
    birth_year_in_range = between(birth_year_number, 1990L, 2024L),
    birth_year_suspect = !birth_year_has_four_digits | !birth_year_in_range,
    birth_year_suspect = replace_na(birth_year_suspect, TRUE),
    sex_unknown = !sex %in% c("F", "M")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    identity_uncertain = breed_unknown | birth_year_suspect | sex_unknown | zipcode_invalid
  ) ->
  dogs_clean
```

### Select named records
We use named licenses to estimate individual dogs. We report missing names separately by ZIP using all licenses.

```{r}
#| label: select-named-records
dogs_clean |>
  filter(!name_missing) ->
  dogs_named
```

### Estimate individual dogs
We treat licenses with the same full name after formatting, sex, birth year, breed and ZIP as one estimated dog. Within each group, we sort the newest issue date first. A tie goes to the later expiry date, then to the earlier row in the source file. `slice_head(n = 1)` keeps the first license in each sorted group. `license_record_count` records how many licenses that row represents. For example, the two matching TOTORO licenses were issued in 2019 and 2024. The 2024 row represents both.

```{r}
#| label: estimate-individual-dogs
dog_key <- c("name_key", "sex", "birth_year", "breed", "zipcode")
dogs_named |>
  group_by(name_key, sex, birth_year, breed, zipcode) |>
  mutate(
    license_record_count = n(),
    original_name_variants = n_distinct(original_name),
    any_compound_name = any(compound_name),
    latest_issue_date = max(license_issue_date),
    latest_issue_ties = sum(license_issue_date == latest_issue_date)
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(license_issue_date), desc(license_expiry_date), source_row_id, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 1) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    retained_row_label = str_pad(source_row_id, width = 6, pad = "0"),
    estimated_dog_id = str_c("dog2024-", retained_row_label)
  ) |>
  arrange(source_row_id) ->
  dogs_estimated
```

```{r}
#| label: estimate-individual-dogs-preview
dogs_estimated |>
  select(estimated_dog_id, original_name, license_record_count) |>
  preview()
```

## Which baby names were popular?
### Read the selected SSA years
The Social Security Administration (SSA) publishes one file per birth year with a name, sex and national birth count. We read the ten files for each of the 1920s, 1970s and 2010s and give names the same spelling rules we used for the dogs.

```{r}
#| label: read-the-selected-ssa-years
ssa_years <- c(1920:1929, 1970:1979, 2010:2019)
ssa_archive_files <- paste0("yob", ssa_years, ".txt")
ssa_extract_directory <- tempfile("barkonomics-ssa-")
dir.create(ssa_extract_directory)
unzip("data/raw/ssa-names.zip", files = ssa_archive_files, exdir = ssa_extract_directory)
ssa_file_paths <- file.path(ssa_extract_directory, ssa_archive_files)
ssa_raw <- read_csv(
  ssa_file_paths,
  col_names = c("name", "sex", "births"),
  col_types = cols(name = col_character(), sex = col_character(), births = col_integer()),
  id = "source_file", na = character()
)
ssa_raw |>
  mutate(
    source_filename = basename(source_file),
    name_key = str_to_upper(name, locale = "en")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    year = str_extract(source_filename, "[0-9]{4}"),
    name_key = str_remove_all(name_key, "[\\s-]")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    year = as.integer(year),
    decade = (year %/% 10L) * 10L
  ) |>
  select(name_key, sex, year, decade, births) ->
  ssa_yearly
```

### Rank names within decades
For each name, add births across years and both sex categories. Order the names by that total within each decade and take the first 100. Alphabetical order breaks ties. The share for each name uses the total number of births in the published counts.

```{r}
#| label: rank-names-within-decades
ssa_yearly |>
  group_by(name_key, decade) |>
  summarise(births = sum(births), .groups = "drop") |>
  group_by(decade) |>
  arrange(desc(births), name_key, .by_group = TRUE, .locale = "C") |>
  mutate(rank = row_number(), share = births / sum(births), top100 = rank <= 100L) |>
  ungroup() ->
  ssa_decades
```

```{r}
#| label: rank-names-within-decades-preview
ssa_decades |>
  filter(rank <= 5)
```

### Make one reference row per name
Give each name one row with a column for each decade’s top-100 result. A dog can then match several decades in one row. A name absent from a decade has zero published births there and no rank.

```{r}
#| label: make-one-reference-row-per-name
ssa_decades |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = decade, values_from = c(births, share, rank, top100),
    values_fill = list(births = 0L, share = 0, top100 = FALSE)
  ) |>
  mutate(ssa_recognized = TRUE) |>
  arrange(name_key, .locale = "C") ->
  ssa_reference
```

## Compare dog names with baby names
### Match names
Each dog keeps its row. A name can appear in the SSA files without making a top-100 list.

```{r}
#| label: join-name-flags-onto-dogs
name_flags <- c("ssa_recognized", "top100_1920", "top100_1970", "top100_2010")
ssa_reference |>
  select(name_key, all_of(name_flags)) ->
  ssa_name_flags

dogs_estimated |>
  left_join(ssa_name_flags, by = "name_key") |>
  mutate(
    ssa_recognized = replace_na(ssa_recognized, FALSE),
    top100_1920 = replace_na(top100_1920, FALSE),
    top100_1970 = replace_na(top100_1970, FALSE),
    top100_2010 = replace_na(top100_2010, FALSE)
  ) |>
  select(
    estimated_dog_id, source_row_id, extract_year, original_name, name_key,
    sex, birth_year, breed, original_zipcode, zipcode,
    license_issue_date, license_expiry_date, license_record_count,
    original_name_variants, latest_issue_ties, compound_name, any_compound_name,
    breed_unknown, birth_year_suspect, sex_unknown, zipcode_padded, zipcode_invalid,
    identity_uncertain, all_of(name_flags)
  ) ->
  dogs
```

```{r}
#| label: join-name-flags-onto-dogs-preview
dogs |>
  select(original_name, all_of(name_flags)) |>
  preview()
```

### Trace source records to dogs
Keep a row-by-row explanation of which source records were consolidated or lacked a name.

```{r}
#| label: trace-source-records-to-dogs
dogs |>
  select(all_of(dog_key), estimated_dog_id, retained_source_row_id = source_row_id) ->
  dog_identity_lookup

dogs_clean |>
  left_join(dog_identity_lookup, by = dog_key) |>
  mutate(
    record_status = case_when(
      name_missing ~ "missing_name",
      source_row_id == retained_source_row_id ~ "retained",
      TRUE ~ "consolidated"
    )
  ) |>
  select(source_row_id, estimated_dog_id, retained_source_row_id, record_status) ->
  license_to_dog
```

### Summarize source missingness
Each license contributes once to the missing-name share for its ZIP.

```{r}
#| label: summarize-source-missingness
dogs_clean |>
  group_by(extract_year, zipcode) |>
  summarise(
    source_license_records = n(), missing_name_records = sum(name_missing),
    named_license_records = sum(!name_missing),
    missing_name_share = mean(name_missing), .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(zipcode) ->
  missing_by_zip

dogs_clean |>
  filter(name_missing) |>
  count(original_name, name = "source_license_records", sort = TRUE) ->
  missing_name_counts
```

```{r}
#| label: summarize-source-missingness-preview
missing_name_counts
```

### Summarize quality flags
```{r}
#| label: summarize-quality-flags
quality_flags <- c("breed_unknown", "birth_year_suspect", "sex_unknown",
  "zipcode_padded", "zipcode_invalid", "identity_uncertain", "compound_name")
dogs_named |>
  summarise(across(all_of(quality_flags), sum)) |>
  mutate(unit = "named_license_record") ->
  license_quality_counts

dogs |>
  summarise(across(all_of(quality_flags), sum)) |>
  mutate(unit = "estimated_dog") ->
  dog_quality_counts

license_quality_counts |>
  bind_rows(dog_quality_counts) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(quality_flags), names_to = "flag", values_to = "count") |>
  select(unit, flag, count) ->
  quality_summary
```

```{r}
#| label: summarize-quality-flags-preview
quality_summary
```

### Inspect the top-100 cutoff
Compare the birth counts for the last name inside each top 100 and the first name outside it.

```{r}
#| label: inspect-the-top-100-cutoff
ssa_decades |>
  filter(rank %in% c(100L, 101L)) |>
  select(decade, rank, name_key, births) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = rank, values_from = c(name_key, births)) |>
  mutate(cutoff_tied = births_100 == births_101) ->
  ssa_cutoffs

ssa_cutoffs
```

### Compare counting units
Compare the share of matching names when each dog counts once with the share when each license counts once.

```{r}
#| label: compare-counting-units
dogs |>
  summarise(across(all_of(name_flags), mean)) |>
  mutate(unit = "estimated_dog") ->
  dog_matching_rates

dogs |>
  summarise(
    ssa_recognized = weighted.mean(ssa_recognized, license_record_count),
    top100_1920 = weighted.mean(top100_1920, license_record_count),
    top100_1970 = weighted.mean(top100_1970, license_record_count),
    top100_2010 = weighted.mean(top100_2010, license_record_count)
  ) |>
  mutate(unit = "named_license_record") ->
  license_matching_rates

dog_matching_rates |>
  bind_rows(license_matching_rates) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(name_flags), names_to = "measure", values_to = "share") |>
  select(unit, measure, share) ->
  matching_comparison

matching_comparison
```

### Save the derived tables
```{r}
#| label: save-the-derived-tables
# Create the folder for the CSVs if needed.
dir.create("data/derived", showWarnings = FALSE)
write_csv(dogs, "data/derived/dogs_2024.csv", na = "")
write_csv(ssa_reference, "data/derived/ssa_name_reference.csv", na = "")
write_csv(ssa_decades, "data/derived/ssa_name_decades.csv", na = "")
write_csv(license_to_dog, "data/derived/license_to_dog.csv", na = "")
write_csv(missing_by_zip, "data/derived/missing_names_by_zip.csv", na = "")
write_csv(missing_name_counts, "data/derived/missing_name_labels.csv", na = "")
write_csv(quality_summary, "data/derived/quality_flags.csv", na = "")
write_csv(ssa_cutoffs, "data/derived/ssa_top100_cutoffs.csv", na = "")
write_csv(matching_comparison, "data/derived/matching_by_counting_unit.csv", na = "")
```

## What changes when we count dogs?
Among estimated dogs, 78.65% have a name that appears in the U.S. baby-name files for the selected years. Counting each named license separately gives 78.78%. Dogs can share all five identifying fields, and changes in a dog’s recorded details can split its licenses across groups. The two percentages show how much the grouping rule matters citywide.

The SSA files omit rare names and have less complete coverage for early births. An unmatched dog name could still be a human name.
